title: Show HN: DeepSeek V3 in ~200 lines of pure Jax
lede: A from-scratch rebuild of the DeepSeek-V3 architecture in about 190 lines of plain JAX, trained on a MacBook Air using public-domain detective novels.

points: Implements MLA attention, DeepSeekMoE, auxiliary-loss-free load balancing and multi-token prediction, with parameters as plain dicts and no Flax or PyTorch.
The model is 36.2M parameters with six layers and a 256-token context, against 671B parameters and 61 layers in the original.
Switching the balancing bias on or off left validation loss almost identical at step 2000, matching the paper's claim.
Simplifications include dense expert compute and no MLA weight absorption; FP8, DualPipe and post-training are left out.
Runs on Apple Silicon through jax-metal, on CPU with a smaller config, and on AMD GPUs through ROCm.

points.text: Commenters welcome it as a learning project, and several say they plan to rebuild it themselves to understand the architecture.
An RX 7600 XT owner got it training on Fedora with ROCm after two environment-variable workarounds, prompting a reply about weak AMD support on consumer cards.
Newcomers ask for a learning path; replies point to 3Blue1Brown and Welch Labs videos and Karpathy's build-from-scratch tutorials.
One commenter suggests standard datasets over detective fiction so results can be compared, and the author agrees.
